thread:
Maya: Quick sync — customer X wants per-tenant encrypted prefetch + HSM-backed keys for private deploys. Need to agree on launch criteria, sequencing, and owners across product/eng/runtime/infra/security. (TL;DR: we can ship a soft-gated pilot in 6 weeks if infra/security can sign the HSM integration by week 3.)

Jules: +1. Can you spell out the hard blockers?

Maya: Blockers: 1) HSM/KMS integration and key policy review (security) 2) Dedicated prewarm slots & autoscale policy for tenant bursts (infra) 3) Runtime KV cache changes to support per-tenant encrypted prefixes (eng-runtime) 4) Acceptance tests for regression on latency/cost (product + SRE)

Kai: From runtime POV, the KV changes look small but need a migration path for existing caches — prefer a canary where new prefixing is opt-in per-tenant.

Sam: Infra: capacity is doable but we need to reserve burst slots. Cost model: prewarm per-tenant increases baseline by ~8% unless we enable smarter eviction. Need exact numbers for customer pricing.

Riley: Security: HSM integration timeline depends on KMS policy review + HSM vendor onboarding. Nominally 2–3 weeks, but if we need FIPS attestation add extra. Also need audit log spec.

Jordan: Product: acceptance criteria proposal: 1) No regression >10% P95 latency; 2) Billing visibility per-tenant; 3) HSM keys provable in audit log; 4) Canary with 5 customers for 2 weeks. Thoughts?

Maya: That aligns. For rollout sequencing I propose: Week 1: finalize spec & owner signoffs; Week 2–3: security + infra onboarding; Week 3–4: runtime dev + internal canary; Week 5–6: external pilot + monitoring; Week 7: GA decision.

Jules: Who owns the spec doc and the rollout playbook? Need a single source of truth.

Maya: I'll own the spec doc draft, Jordan will own acceptance tests, Kai owns rollout canary toggles, Sam owns infra reservations, Riley owns security signoff checklist.

Kai: For the canary toggle I suggest a per-tenant flag and a rollout script. Example config snippet: ```json
{
  "tenant_id": "T-123",
  "prefetch": { "enabled": true, "encrypted_prefix": "v2" },
  "canary": true
}
```

Sam: We also need a cost cap guardrail in infra to prevent runaway prewarm charging during canary. Suggest a soft quota linked to billing alert.

Riley: Security checklist (short): KMS policy drafted, HSM vendor credentialed, audit logging enabled, PIIs checked, threat model signoff. I'll post the doc by EOD.

Jordan: For acceptance tests — we should include a small workload that exercises heavy KV cache hits and simulated tenant bursts. I'll add perf thresholds to the test harness.

Maya: Timeline risk flags: if security needs vendor procurement, +2–3 weeks. If runtime refactor hits an edge case with eviction, +1–2 weeks. Need triage plan for both.

Jules: Recommend a fallback policy: if HSM not ready, allow software KMS with explicit customer opt-in and a stricter SLA. That buys time.

Riley: We can allow soft KMS fallback but must mark it clearly in billing & contract. Security ok with that path if customer signs waiver.

Kai: Agreed. We'll implement the toggle so customer can choose HSM vs software keys at tenant level.

Maya: Action items: Maya -> spec draft by Tue, Jordan -> acceptance tests scaffold by Wed, Kai -> canary toggle PR by Fri, Sam -> capacity reservation estimate by Thu, Riley -> security checklist + HSM vendor note by EOD.

Sam: Noted. I'll push a capacity estimate to the doc and include cost delta scenarios.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: Reminder: feature-flag infra quota change scheduled for Saturday 02:00 UTC, will require a short infra freeze window.

Maya: Thanks — we'll aim to avoid conflicting changes during that window. If infra freeze conflicts with PR timelines we can shift canary.

Jordan: I'll coordinate with SRE on monitoring dashboards: token-level latency, prewarm billing, and per-tenant error rate.

Maya: Great — last call: any showstopper objections?

Jules: None from product. Keep tight on acceptance tests. :thumbsup:

Kai: No blockers from runtime besides the migration plan — I'll put a risk doc in the spec.

Riley: No blockers but vendor procurement is highest risk.

Sam: No blockers; will confirm numbers in the doc.

Maya: Cool — thanks everyone. I'll post the spec link when done and ping for signoffs.
